questions.question: Distracted driving can be caused by:

options.text: Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.

questions.explanation: Drivers make about 200 decisions for every mile they drive. It is important to focus completely on driving. Any other activity can be a dangerous distraction.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal well in advance. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check your blind spot.

questions.question: A green arrow with a red light means:

options.text: You can only drive straight ahead.
You can only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to go any direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only drive in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow appears with a red light, you can only drive in the direction the arrow points. The intersection must be clear before you proceed.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look in your rearview and side mirrors to see if anyone is passing you. Also look over your shoulder to make sure no one is in your blind spot.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, you must show:
questions.explanation: You must have your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance in your vehicle at all times. You must show all three documents when stopped.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Look over your shoulder for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Check both your side and rearview mirrors for traffic behind you. Just before moving into the other lane, look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: Which must you obey over the other three?
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions take priority over all traffic signs and signals. Police officers, fire police, highway work zone flaggers, and school crossing guards can direct traffic.

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and give them the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to prevent injury.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is someone who:

options.text: Looks away from the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at a passenger instead of the road during conversation.
Only watches the vehicle directly ahead.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by passengers, searching for items in your vehicle, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming. Keep scanning the road, checking mirrors, and looking at your instrument panel regularly. These habits will help you stay alert while driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A volunteer group is picking up trash on the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that workers may be on or near the roadway ahead. Drive carefully through the work zone.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving

questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign:

options.text: Drive faster than the train to cross safely.
Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Keep driving normally. No trains are nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs warn you that a train may be coming. Always obey these signs. Never go around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: How much space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
Whether there is a stop sign.
Whether you use your turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: How lack of sleep affects your driving is the same as:

options.text: How driving with teenagers affects your driving.

questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol have similar effects on driving. Being awake for 18 hours impairs driving like a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours impairs driving like a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you?
questions.explanation: Alcohol impairs the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. It slows your reaction time, balance, and coordination. It also weakens your vision and your ability to judge distance.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate lowers.
Ignore how many tracks you need to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When approaching railroad tracks, look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop for trains or other vehicles using the tracks.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep your tires at the correct air pressure.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your vehicle slides on a layer of water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure, worn tires, and speeding all increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: Seat belts work best when worn by:

options.text: Everyone in the car every time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone in the car every time.
questions.explanation: Everyone in your vehicle should wear a seat belt every time you drive. Without a seat belt, a person becomes a flying object in a crash and can injure others.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if possible. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Help stop severe bleeding with pressure. Wait for emergency vehicles.

questions.question: A reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means:
questions.explanation: A reflective orange triangle on a vehicle means it is traveling slower than 25 mph. You may see this on farm equipment, construction vehicles, and horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that traffic only moves in one direction. You must drive in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires cause three problems: they make turning harder, they increase how far you need to stop, and they are more likely to hydroplane on wet roads.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while you are driving. You should:

options.text: Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
Turn on your emergency flashers and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not brake suddenly. Grip the wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Slowly take your foot off the gas and reduce your speed. When you are going very slowly, gently apply the brakes and pull to the side of the road safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means yield. Slow down and let other traffic go first. Stop only if necessary.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and opposing traffic is blocking your view. You should:

options.text: Accelerate rapidly when the first lane you need to cross is clear.
Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before going ahead with your turn.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across the intersection.
Edge your car into each lane of opposing traffic as soon as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before going ahead with your turn.
questions.explanation: Never turn left until you can see that all lanes are clear. Make sure you can safely complete the turn before you go.

questions.question: Highway markings:

options.text: Are only found in construction zones.
Are usually red and blue in color.

questions.explanation: Highway markings give you information. They show you where to position your car, where you can pass safely, and warn you about road changes ahead.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate:

options.text: Stop on the shoulder of the road if you are tired.
You should always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, look in your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes. Stop on the shoulder only in emergencies. Avoid using cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather. Change lanes only when needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection. Do not make a right turn where this sign is posted.

questions.question: To ensure that your physical condition does not cause you to drive in an unsafe manner, you should:

options.text: Keep physically fit and have regular physical examinations.
Know the effect of any medicine on your driving ability.

questions.explanation: Your physical health affects your driving safety. Stay in good shape, get regular checkups, know how medicines affect you, and only drive when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When driving on slick roads, you should:

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, slow down for turns and curves. Going too fast in turns on wet or icy roads is especially dangerous.
